stage1.impression: A glowing acrylic column on a wood table at night, but the room is lit as evenly as the lamp, so it reads as a lamp switched on in a lit room rather than the light source; the red core clips into a flat bar, the tinted strata go muddy dark red, and the black foot disappears. The cropped white vase at the right edge is the second-brightest thing in the frame and pulls the eye out of it.

blocking_9: The lamp has to be the key: the table directly in front of it (700,890,900,1000) at least 2x the luminance of the far table (1050,900,1400,1060). Now it is 49.5 vs 46.9, so there is effectively no pool.
The wall should fall off from the lamp instead of being one value. Now it is 49.6 with a range of 3.1 at the top left and 45.3 with a range of 4.1 at the top right.
The glowing core must hold tone. Now 44% of (765,420,840,720) is clipped in R (r_median 253).
The disc strata need edge light so the separate discs and their clear and satin finishes read. Now the sides are lum 15 to 17 with g 2 to 4: a uniform dark red with no visible faces.
The anodised foot needs a readable edge. Now 79% of (640,770,930,870) is crushed (median 2.4).
No bright prop cut by the frame edge (the vase at x 1430 to 1600, median 70).

changes.problem: The room fill lights the table and wall as evenly as the lamp does, so the lamp's coloured light on the table, which is the point of the frame, does not show.

evidence.measured: far table lum_median 46.9 vs 49.5 directly in front of the lamp (700,890,900,1000); table profile x 400 to 1300 is 48.3, 49.1, 47.0, 45.5, 43.7, 44.2, 45.1, 44.9, with no peak under the lamp; wall 49.6 with a range of 3.1

changes.expected: The far table and wall drop to about 20 to 30, so the lamp's own spill becomes the brightest thing on the table and wall.

changes.problem: The lamp throws too little light to make a visible warm pool on the oak in front of it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 49.5, r 82, g 42, b 23; barely warmer than the far table (r 67, g 43)

changes.expected: A warm amber-red pool on the table in front of the foot, at about twice the far table's level, warmer in R.

changes.problem: The red core is clipped in R into a flat bar with no gradient along the tube.
changes.expected: The core holds tone: R below 245 across most of the tube and a visible falloff between the discs, while the glow raised in c2 keeps the pool.

changes.problem: Seen from outside, the disc stack has no edge light, so the bonded discs and their buffed and bead-blasted finishes read as one dark red mass.

evidence.measured: lum_median 15.1, p95 28.4, r 61, g 2, b 0; left side (610,400,700,680) 15.6 with a range of 13.3

change.to: narrow vertical strip softbox, about 15 x 60 cm, 5000 K, behind the lamp and about 120 degrees to camera right at disc height, about 0.8 m from the lamp, about 30% of the original fill's watts

changes.expected: A thin bright edge down the right silhouette of the stack, with the disc joints catching as separate lines and the satin discs glowing softer than the clear ones. The sides rise to a p95 of about 50 to 90 without lifting the front faces much.

changes.problem: The black anodised foot is crushed to pure black, so the lamp seems to float on a hole.

change.to: white card about 20 x 8 cm, standing on the table about 25 cm in front and left of the lamp, out of frame below camera; or a weak 2 cm strip light at table height giving one horizontal highlight on the foot's chamfer

changes.expected: One soft highlight along the foot's front edge and its knurled-knob side, with the foot body still deep black.

changes.problem: The white vase is cut by the right frame edge and is the brightest thing after the lamp, so it competes with the hero.

change.to: remove vase; place two pears on a plate about 30 cm behind and right of the lamp, fully in frame, below the lamp's mid-height

changes.expected: The right edge of the frame becomes dark wall and table, and the only secondary object is small, low and lit by the lamp.

changes.problem: The room is a single warm brown (wall r 62, g 47, b 39), so the warm lamp has no cool dusk to stand against.
changes.expected: The wall reads as dark cool slate, about lum 22 to 30, so the lamp's amber and red are the only warm tones.

out_of_scope.request: Make the seven amber discs read amber rather than deep red (sides measure g 2 to 4; delta E 2000 of 46 against #C8781E).
out_of_scope.why: The tints are calibrated to transmission, so thick parts go deep. The rim light in c4 may bring some amber out at the edges, but the body colour is fixed.

out_of_scope.request: Soften the hard bright rectangle of the opal tube behind the frosted top (745,200,855,370: median 202 against 54 to 57 beside it).
out_of_scope.why: It is the lamp's design and its bead-blasted finish. Lighting cannot change it, and it dominates the top third.
